# Latency-Sensitive Tensor Offloading Plan for Nemotron-H on 12GB GPU

## Executive Summary
To maintain interactive latency on a 12GB GPU while supporting the full Nemotron-H MoE architecture, we must offload **Mamba2 SSM tensors**, **attention tensors**, **router logits**, and **shared-expert FFN tensors** to CPU RAM. The 12GB constraint forces selective offloading: keep the heaviest MoE expert weights on CPU, but retain critical path tensors (QKV, output projection, MLP gate) on GPU to avoid per-token router computation overhead.

---

## 1. Tensor Offloading Strategy

### Tensors to Keep on GPU (latency-critical path)
| Tensor Name | Shape | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `tok_embd` | `{n_embd, n_vocab}` | Embedding lookup is unavoidable; kept on GPU for throughput |
| `output_norm.weight` | `{n_embd}` | Final RMSNorm; tiny, always on GPU |
| `output.weight` / `output` (duplicated) | `{n_embd, n_vocab}` | LM head; must be on GPU for logit computation |
| `layers[i].attn_norm.weight` | `{n_embd}` | Attention pre-norm; essential for every token |
| `layers[i].wo.weight` | `{n_embd_head_k * n_head_i, n_embd}` | Attention output projection; high-frequency access |
| `layers[i].ffn_down.weight` / `ffn_up.weight` (non-MoE) | `{n_ff, n_embd}` / `{n_embd, n_ff}` | Standard MLP; kept on GPU for non-MoE layers |
| `layers[i].ffn_gate_inp.weight` | `{n_embd, n_expert}` | **Router gate**; must stay on GPU to avoid CPU↔GPU transfer per token |

| Tensor Name | Shape | Offload Target |
|---|---|---|
| `layers[i].ssm_in.weight` | `{n_embd, d_in_proj}` | CPU RAM (large, per-layer) |
